QF.id: XC Investment Products and Market Developments_6

question.text: Per the SEBI hybrid scheme categorisation referenced in the NISM Series X-A workbook (p.212), which hybrid mutual fund category is specifically defined to invest between 65% and 80% of its assets in equity and equity-related instruments and 20% to 35% in debt instruments?

answer.text: Balanced Advantage Fund (dynamic asset allocation, with no fixed 65-80% equity band)
Equity Savings Fund (minimum 65% equity, but the equity portion includes large unhedged plus hedged exposure)
Arbitrage Fund (maintains 65% equity through hedged positions for taxation, not as a directional aggressive-hybrid allocation)

explanation.text: The Logic: The SEBI hybrid scheme categorisation summarised in NISM Series X-A (p.212) defines an Aggressive Hybrid Fund as a hybrid scheme investing 65-80% in equity and 20-35% in debt. By tightening the stem to that exact 65-80% / 20-35% band, Aggressive Hybrid Fund is the uniquely correct category. The Trap: Balanced Advantage Funds dynamically shift between equity and debt without a fixed 65-80% band. Equity Savings Funds maintain at least 65% equity but rely heavily on hedged exposure rather than a defined 65-80% directional band. Arbitrage Funds maintain ~65% equity but only through hedged positions for taxation. The audit flagged the original because the prior stem asked broadly which scheme invests "a minimum of 65% in equity", which could match aggressive hybrid, equity savings, ELSS, balanced advantage (under the taxation lens), or even pure equity funds. Note: The original stem asked broadly about "minimum 65% equity" and offered "pure equity fund" - language that matched multiple workbook-defined categories. The stem now targets the precise 65-80% equity / 20-35% debt band that the workbook defines as Aggressive Hybrid Fund (NISM Series X-A p.212), making that the uniquely correct answer.
